## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
*Kusalattika, Vedanāttika* is a text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna* within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. As the first triad-combination chapter, it synthesizes the wholesome triad (*kusalattika*) with the feeling triad (*vedanāttika*) [Nyanatiloka 2007]. Its opening exposition in the chapter on conditionality or dependence (*paṭiccavāra*) analyzes conditional relations, such as how, dependent on a wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling, there may arise a wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling, conditioned by way of root (*hetupaccaya*) [Nyanatiloka 2007].
No curated parallels are recorded on SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches meeting the threshold [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus does, however, record widespread Pali-internal textual reuse across the Abhidhamma literature, amounting to 1,163 matching passages across 89 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive correspondences are with other treatments of the same triad pairing (*Kusalattika, Vedanāttika*, Patthana 11.1 and Patthana 17.1), the reverse pairing (*Vedanāttika, Kusalattika*, Patthana 11.10 and Patthana 23.20), as well as related triad analysis sections such as Patthana 5.1 and Patthana 13.2 [DharmaNexus].
